title: USB VIP agent/component class hierarchy and callback mechanism -- svt_usb_agent internals + svt_usb_protocol_callbacks flow
summary: Component hierarchy (UVM guide Sec 4.2.1-4.2.3 lines 1789-2176; HDL guide Sec 3.1.1 lines 571-617): uvm_agent -> svt_usb_agent (top-level, models Host/Device/Hub) containing sequencer+driver+monitor (TLM pull-port; xactor drivers pull via sequence_item_pull_port). Internally, BOTH UVM and HDL flavors share the same 3-layer transactor stack: svt_usb_protocol (top, breaks transfers into transactions/packets) -> svt_usb_link (LTSSM for SS; USB2.0 reset/suspend/resume state machines) -> svt_usb_physical (bottom, drives PIPE3/serial signaling), plus optional 4th remote_phys transactor only in PIPE3-to-DUT-PHY topologies (not this project's plain-serial topology). Stack top is selectable via config top_xactor property (can drive VIP at link/physical layer directly). Concrete sub-component class names for verbosity/debug targeting (UVM guide Sec 6.1.2.2 table, lines 5002-5047): Protocol-2.0: svt_usb_protocol_20_host_non_isoc_ep_processor, svt_usb_protocol_20_host_isoc_ep_processor, svt_usb_protocol_20_device_non_isoc_ep_processor/_isoc_ep_processor, svt_usb_protocol_20_host, svt_usb_protocol_20_device, svt_usb_protocol_20_lpm_processor, svt_usb_protocol_20_sof_processor. Link-2.0: svt_usb_link_20, svt_usb_link_20_device_a_sm (Host/A-device role), svt_usb_link_20_device_b_sm (Device/B-device role), svt_usb_link_20_timer. Since this project's VIP=Host, active classes are the *_20_host_*_ep_processor and svt_usb_link_20_device_a_sm. VIP's own log search strings: 'L20_DEV_A_SM' when VIP acts as Host/A-device (e.g. 'uvm_test_top.env.host_agent.link.usb_20_device_a ... L20_DEV_A_SM: DEVICE_ATTACHED <- DISCONNECTED' then '-> RESETTING'), 'L20_DEV_B_SM' when VIP acts as Device/B-device (FAQ Sec 2.2.3, lines 1061-1099) -- direct grep target for USB2.0 link-state debug in this project's sim logs. UVM base classes actually used: uvm_agent, uvm_component, uvm_object, uvm_callback, uvm_sequencer -- no custom component-model primitives. CALLBACK MECHANISM (UVM guide Sec 4.2.2 lines 1823-1848, Sec 4.2.3.5 lines 2122-2176, Sec 4.2.9 lines 3095-3556): three callback classes: svt_usb_link_callbacks, svt_usb_physical_callbacks, svt_usb_protocol_callbacks (extends svt_xactor_callbacks -> uvm_callback). Virtual/empty by default -- zero cost unless registered via uvm_callbacks#(svt_usb_protocol)::add(agent.prot, my_cb). Three call-site categories: post-port-get, pre-port-put, traffic/dataflow-event. Coverage callbacks fire after get/put UNLESS that method set drop_it=1. Concrete method inventory: post_transfer_in_port_get(component,port_id,transfer,ref bit drop) -- right after pulling from transfer_in, drop=1 skips coverage; transfer_in_port_cov(...) -- coverage sample point; randomized_transaction(component,transfer,transaction_ix,rand_point) -- fires on every host_response/device_response randomization, THE hook for overriding response behavior (FAQ Sec 3.1.6 lines 1312-1350 gives full retry_ack_callback example mutating xact.rty_bit_0_in_resend_of_ack_after_retry_ack based on xact.last_pkt_sent.tp_subpacket_type/.rty_bit); received_data_packet(component,transfer,packet) -- error-free DATA received; transaction_ended(component,transfer,transaction_ix); transfer_ended(component,transfer); pre_usb_20_packet_out_port_put(component,chan_id,packet,transaction,packet_ix,transfer,transaction_ix,ref bit drop) -- pre-put hook for mutating packet.payload.data[] before it leaves protocol layer (FAQ Sec 1.22 lines 852-905 gives full modify_ctrl_read_data_callback example patching a DEVICE_TO_HOST control-read response); parallel pre_usb_SS_packet_out_port_put() for USB3.x (named only, not detailed in this doc set). Full Host-role (=this project's VIP role) non-iso callback/event sequence documented step-by-step in UVM guide Sec 4.2.9.1.1 (lines 3095-3244): transfer_in port get -> exception-list randomization -> post_transfer_in_port_get -> transfer_in_port_cov -> per-transaction TOKEN send -> DATA/HANDSHAKE receive -> branch by type (Device IN DATA / Device HANDSHAKE for OUT / for SETUP) each converging on transaction.status=ACCEPT, transfer.end_tr(), svt_usb_protocol::NOTIFY_USB_TRANSACTION_ENDED.trigger(transaction.clone) -- universal max-error-budget abort check after every branch. Device-role flow (Sec 4.2.9.2, lines 3347-3556, relevant only if a passive/loopback Device agent is added) starts from packet_in_port (not transfer_in) and inserts a 'Randomize Transaction for Response' callback flow (sets device_response) before every branch. HDL/command-interface flavor uses a DIFFERENT synchronous mechanism, not uvm_callback: cmd_callback_wait_for(is_valid,out_handle,'prot.NOTIFY_CB_<event>') blocks and returns a data-object handle; cmd_callback_proceed(...) is the release handshake. Hard constraint: simulation time must not advance between wait_for and proceed or a FATAL is reported (HDL guide Sec 2.1.2, lines 417-463). Example: NOTIFY_CB_NEW_SS_RESPONSE_TRANSFER.
